newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Goodale to consider extending barley vote.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Goodale to consider extending barley vote.

text.p: Canadian Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale is prepared to extend the deadline for a vote on barley marketing if it turns out many farmers have had trouble voting, his spokesman Vern Greenshields said on Friday.

The Alberta Grain Commission urged the federal government to extend today's deadline for voting on whether farmers wished to keep the Canadian Wheat Board's monopoly on barley exports or sell in the open market.
The commission said numerous farmers had been unable to get their ballots mailed on time.
"He (Goodale) said that he will be evaluating over the weekend and finding out the severity of the problem," Greenshields said.

"But he wanted to stress that people should have the opportunity to vote. So, if there's a significant problem, he'll be looking at an extension, but right now we have to determine the severity of the problem," Greenshields said.
